subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime callers permanently fail closed on every legacy ownerless session row, or must OpenClaw provide a one-time migration or explicit operator adoption path before enforcing this boundary?
rationale: Source inspection establishes the isolation benefit, but repository policy treats persisted-state compatibility and fallback removal as maintainer-owned decisions because existing plugin workflows can stop after upgrade.

options.title: Fail closed with recovery
options.body: Reject ownerless rows and document a safe operator or doctor path for handling affected legacy sessions.

options.title: Migrate safe ownership
options.body: Add a narrowly defined doctor migration when ownership can be established without letting plugins adopt arbitrary rows.

options.title: Limit the first fix
options.body: Reject only explicitly foreign-owned rows now and defer ownerless-row policy to a separately reviewed security change.

recommendation.title: Fail closed with recovery
recommendation.body: Reject ownerless rows and document a safe operator or doctor path for handling affected legacy sessions.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history ties him to the existing ownership fence and session projection architecture that define this policy boundary.
